abstract: Ribosome profiling is a powerful method for transcriptome-wide monitoring of translation activity in vivo, but its use is limited by lengthy protocols, reliance on specialized equipment and inefficient recovery of ribosome-protected fragments (RPFs). To overcome these challenges, we developed RAPPL-Seq, a magnetic bead-based affinity capture method that enables fast and efficient RPF isolation. RAPPL-Seq achieves high recovery efficiency, short processing time, and robust performance with limited input material. It is broadly applicable across multiple sample types, including cell lines, primary tissues, and human biospecimens. RAPPL-Seq can also be paired with translation inhibitors to characterize inhibitor- and tissue-specific mRNA translation. RAPPL-Seq efficiently captured translatomes of glioblastoma (GBM) and adjacent non-tumor brain tissues from patient biopsies. Together, these findings establish RAPPL-Seq as a straightforward, easily accessible, and highly sensitive approach that extends translatome studies to scarce experimental and clinical samples, opening new avenues for mechanistic insight and therapeutic discovery.
